security_audit.summary: Most markdown code fence detections are false positives from examples, but the documentation includes privileged installation, pipe-to-shell setup, and secret handling risks. The skill also describes automated computational execution, so generated methods and credentials require sandboxing and human review.

remediation.suggestion: Replace `curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash` with package manager steps, checksum verification, or vendor documentation links.
Pin Docker images by digest, document image ownership, and prefer secret managers or least-privilege keys over `--env-file`.
Replace `echo $OPENAI_API_KEY` with checks that confirm variable presence without showing the value.
Offer non-root alternatives, smaller TeX packages, or Docker isolation, and warn users before any `sudo` command.
Require review of generated methodology and run Denario results in a sandbox with limited files, network, and credentials.
Avoid adding sensitive credential paths to shell startup files unless users understand the exposure and rotation plan.

content.value_statement: Scientific research workflows often require repeated handoffs between ideas, methods, analysis, and writing. This skill guides Denario workflows for assisted research planning, execution, and manuscript drafting.
actual_capabilities: Explains Denario installation with uv, pip, source builds, and Docker.
Guides LLM credential setup for OpenAI and Google Vertex AI.
Shows how to define data descriptions, research ideas, methods, and results.
Demonstrates automated generation of analyses, visualizations, and LaTeX papers.
Provides examples for climate, biomedical, time-series, and machine learning studies.
Documents review steps for generated methodology, results, figures, and manuscripts.
limitations: Requires Python 3.12, Denario, and working LLM API credentials.
Generated research outputs require expert review before publication or operational use.
Automated analysis can run code, create files, and consume paid API credits.
Paper generation requires LaTeX or the Docker image with LaTeX installed.

use_cases.title: Accelerate early research planning
use_cases.description: A data scientist turns dataset details into research questions, methods, and validation checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Draft manuscript structure
use_cases.description: An academic researcher converts reviewed methods and results into a journal-style LaTeX paper draft.

use_cases.title: Prototype reproducible analyses
use_cases.description: A research engineer builds a staged project directory with scripts, figures, notes, and manuscript assets.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a Denario project for this dataset: [dataset summary]. List required inputs, credentials, review steps, and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Research Ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Denario to turn this data description into research questions: [description]. Suggest three hypotheses and note supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Methodology
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Denario-generated methodology before running results: [method]. Identify validation gaps, unsafe assumptions, and required human checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Pipeline Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a full Denario workflow for [research goal]. Include sandboxing, credential handling, version control, cost controls, and review gates.

output_examples.input: Dataset summary for global temperature anomalies with pandas, scipy, sklearn, and plotting tools.
output_examples.output: A staged plan with data description improvements, hypothesis options, methodology review points, result validation checks, and manuscript steps.

output_examples.input: Existing methods and results for a traffic optimization study.
output_examples.output: A paper drafting workflow that organizes context, methods, findings, figures, citations, and final LaTeX review tasks.

output_examples.input: A request to launch Denario with cloud model credentials.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist that separates credentials from source control, recommends least privilege, and warns before Docker or shell commands.

best_practices: Review generated ideas, methods, and results before allowing code execution.
Use a virtual environment or isolated container for every research project.
Store credentials outside version control and rotate keys after shared experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated analysis code on sensitive data without sandboxing.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts, logs, commits, or screenshots.
Do not treat generated manuscripts as publication-ready without domain review.

faq.question: Does this skill install Denario automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users still choose and run installation commands.

faq.question: Does Denario require API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Denario needs supported LLM provider credentials, such as OpenAI or Google Vertex AI keys.

faq.question: Can it create a complete paper?
faq.answer: It can draft LaTeX source and a paper structure from reviewed research outputs.

faq.question: Should I run generated code directly?
faq.answer: No. Review generated methodology and code first, then run it in an isolated environment.

faq.question: Can I use existing results?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide existing ideas, methods, and results before generating a manuscript.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are credential exposure, cloud costs, generated code execution, Docker images, and privileged installation commands.
